# The Autumn Sign That Remains

## Scripture
"As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease." — Genesis 8:22

## Reflection
By early September, the constellation Lyra—the harp—now ascends high in the eastern sky after sunset. Its brightest star, Vega, has been called the "summer star," yet it lingers well into autumn, a fixed point in a turning sky. While the seasons shift around us, Vega doesn't move; it simply becomes part of a different evening backdrop.

There's something deeply comforting about that constancy. God made this promise to Noah after the flood—not that seasons would be pleasant, but that they would be *reliable*. The cold will come. The harvest will end. The nights will lengthen. But none of this signals chaos; it signals covenant.

We often treat our spiritual seasons the same way we treat weather—as if a dry spell means God has forgotten us. Yet the same God who set Lyra in its place has set *you* in His story. Your winter is not your end. Your seedtime will return. The turning skies above you are not random; they are rehearsals of His faithfulness.

Look up tonight. Vega will be there, as it has been for millennia. And so will the One who holds both the stars and your seasons in His hands.

## Prayer
Faithful Creator, when my seasons feel uncertain, remind me that You are the God who keeps promises. Help me trust the turning, knowing You remain unchanged. Amen.
